raw_response:
I have farmed for a long time, and on 10.1 mu with some labor going off-farm, I will keep the plan steady and practical. I will put most of my land into the wheat-maize rotation because that is the backbone of my farm, it fits Quzhou County well, and I have well irrigation to support it when water is needed. I will keep a smaller piece for chili because chili brings cash, but it also needs more labor and more careful field management, so I will not expand it too much at my age. I will use better seed where it clearly helps yield and stability, keep fertilizer at a level I know the land can carry, irrigate enough to protect the crop but not waste water, and use rotary tillage on the grain land because it is faster and suits my labor situation. For chili, I will manage more intensively with more water, potash, and crop protection because that crop is more sensitive and worth the extra attention.
